question.:question/problem: The least common multiple of $5(w+8)^{2}$ and $9(w+8)^{2}$ is {{field-1}}. Use the positive integer LCM of the contents and a primitive polynomial part with positive leading coefficient.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the least common multiple ($\text{LCM}$) of two polynomials that are made up of products of binomials, we find the least common multiple of the constants and the least common multiple of the variable part. Then, we multiply all of the results together.

So first, we find $\text{LCM}(5,9):$

- Multiples of $5:$ $\,5,\,10,\,15,\,20,\,25,\,30,\,35,\,40,\,45,\,50,…$

- Multiples of $9:$ $\,9,\,18,\,27,\,36,\,45,\,54,…$

So, $\text{LCM}(5,9)=45.$

Since the variable part is the same in the expressions, we have

$$
\text{LCM}((w+8)^{2},\,(w+8)^{2})=(w+8)^{2}.
$$

Finally, we multiply all of our results together:

$$
\text{LCM}(5(w+8)^{2},\,9(w+8)^{2})=45\cdot (w+8)^{2}=45(w+8)^{2}.
$$

generation.convention: positive integer content LCM times common positive-leading primitive part

question.:question/problem: The least common multiple of $18x^{2}-27x-45$ and $-24x^{2}+36x+60$ is {{field-1}}. Use the positive integer LCM of the contents and a primitive polynomial part with positive leading coefficient.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the least common multiple ($\text{LCM}$) of two polynomials that differ by a constant factor, we find the least common multiple of the constants and the least common multiple of the variable part. Then, we multiply all of the results together.

First, factor out the integer contents and identify the common primitive polynomial:

$$
18x^{2}-27x-45=9(2x^{2}-3x-5),\qquad -24x^{2}+36x+60=(-12)(2x^{2}-3x-5).
$$

Use the positive contents $9$ and $12$.

So first, we find $\text{LCM}(9,12):$

- Multiples of $9:$ $\,9,\,18,\,27,\,36,\,45,…$

- Multiples of $12:$ $\,12,\,24,\,36,\,48,…$

So, $\text{LCM}(9,12)=36.$

Since the variable part is the same in the expressions, we have

$$
\text{LCM}((2x^{2}-3x-5),\,(2x^{2}-3x-5))=(2x^{2}-3x-5).
$$

Finally, we multiply all of our results together:

$$
\text{LCM}(18x^{2}-27x-45,\,-24x^{2}+36x+60)=36\cdot (2x^{2}-3x-5)=36(2x^{2}-3x-5).
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the least common multiple of $40x^{2}+90x-80$ and $-60x^{2}-135x+120.$ Use the positive integer LCM of the contents and a primitive polynomial part with positive leading coefficient.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the least common multiple ($\text{LCM}$) of two polynomials that differ by a constant factor, we find the least common multiple of the constants and the least common multiple of the variable part. Then, we multiply all of the results together.

First, factor out the integer contents and identify the common primitive polynomial:

$$
40x^{2}+90x-80=10(4x^{2}+9x-8),\qquad -60x^{2}-135x+120=(-15)(4x^{2}+9x-8).
$$

Use the positive contents $10$ and $15$.

So first, we find $\text{LCM}(10,15):$

- Multiples of $10:$ $\,10,\,20,\,30,\,40,…$

- Multiples of $15:$ $\,15,\,30,\,45,…$

So, $\text{LCM}(10,15)=30.$

Since the variable part is the same in the expressions, we have

$$
\text{LCM}((4x^{2}+9x-8),\,(4x^{2}+9x-8))=(4x^{2}+9x-8).
$$

Finally, we multiply all of our results together:

$$
\text{LCM}(40x^{2}+90x-80,\,-60x^{2}-135x+120)=30\cdot (4x^{2}+9x-8)=30(4x^{2}+9x-8).
$$

generation.convention: positive integer content LCM times common positive-leading primitive part

question.:question/problem: The least common multiple of $42x^{2}+28x+42$ and $-18x^{2}-12x-18$ is {{field-1}}. Use the positive integer LCM of the contents and a primitive polynomial part with positive leading coefficient.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the least common multiple ($\text{LCM}$) of two polynomials that differ by a constant factor, we find the least common multiple of the constants and the least common multiple of the variable part. Then, we multiply all of the results together.

First, factor out the integer contents and identify the common primitive polynomial:

$$
42x^{2}+28x+42=14(3x^{2}+2x+3),\qquad -18x^{2}-12x-18=(-6)(3x^{2}+2x+3).
$$

Use the positive contents $14$ and $6$.

So first, we find $\text{LCM}(14,6):$

- Multiples of $14:$ $\,14,\,28,\,42,\,56,…$

- Multiples of $6:$ $\,6,\,12,\,18,\,24,\,30,\,36,\,42,\,48,…$

So, $\text{LCM}(14,6)=42.$

Since the variable part is the same in the expressions, we have

$$
\text{LCM}((3x^{2}+2x+3),\,(3x^{2}+2x+3))=(3x^{2}+2x+3).
$$

Finally, we multiply all of our results together:

$$
\text{LCM}(42x^{2}+28x+42,\,-18x^{2}-12x-18)=42\cdot (3x^{2}+2x+3)=42(3x^{2}+2x+3).
$$
